claims.claim: The forever block runs its contained code repeatedly as a background task that starts automatically when the program launches and takes no parameters.

show string scrolls the given text one character at a time leftward across the 5x5 LED matrix, accepts a required text string plus an optional interval parameter (milliseconds between characters, default 150ms).
show icon displays a single predefined icon selected from the IconNames enumeration (e.g., Heart, Happy, Sad) on the LED matrix until the next display command, taking one icon-name parameter.
pause suspends execution of the current fiber for a specified number of milliseconds (ms parameter) but does not block other parallel forever loops or registered event handlers.
if/then/else evaluates a Boolean condition and runs the then branch when true or the else branch when false, with both branches being optional in the block editor.
on shake registers an event handler via input.onGesture using the Gesture.Shake value that executes whenever a shake gesture is detected, taking the gesture type as its parameter.
pick random (Math.randomRange) returns a random integer between its two inclusive numeric bounds, so the lower and upper limits are both possible outputs.
input.acceleration, given a Dimension parameter of X, Y, or Z, returns the current acceleration along that axis measured in milli-g (mG).
